objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the improved pulse oximeter with a co-located micro-optical diffuser in low perfusion conditions
dependent_variables: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of blood oxygen saturation readings in low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%)
controls: Current state-of-the-art pulse oximeters without the micro-optical diffuser
Standard clinical protocols for patient monitoring
baseline: Current state-of-the-art pulse oximeters without the micro-optical diffuser
procedure: Recruit 100 patients with low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%)
Measure blood oxygen saturation using both the improved pulse oximeter with the micro-optical diffuser and the current state-of-the-art pulse oximeters
Record the MAE of blood oxygen saturation readings for each device over a testing duration of 30 minutes
Repeat the measurements for each patient to ensure reliable results
expected_result: A 15% decrease in MAE of blood oxygen saturation readings in low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%) compared to the current state-of-the-art pulse oximeters
falsification_condition: A study showing an increase in MAE of at least 20% in low perfusion conditions compared to the current state-of-the-art pulse oximeters
safety_constraints: Ensure that all patients are monitored by a trained medical professional and that the testing procedure does not pose any risk to the patients
information_gain: The effectiveness of the improved pulse oximeter with a co-located micro-optical diffuser in low perfusion conditions, and the potential for improved patient outcomes and reduced medical errors
